messages:
julia: quick idea - introducing a 'soft-stop' intermediate state for staged rollouts. instead of immediate rollback when a signal trips, we stop assigning NEW pilot binds and route new traffic to fallback while we gather diagnostics. want to sync on signals, timing, and the observer->controller event contract :thinking:

rahul: I like a soft-stop. main concerns: noisy signals and oscillation, and per-tenant vs global thresholds. we need hysteresis + safety budget. which signals do we accept? p95 latency, error spike (5xx), and some automated quality eval?

maggie: propose composite triggers to reduce false positives:
- sustained error_rate delta: delta(error_rate, baseline) > 0.5% sustained for 3m
- latency tail: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.4 for 2m
- model quality regression: eval_fail_rate > 2%
include a cooldown (default 10m) and exponential backoff for repeated soft-stops. semantic: soft-stop != rollback. soft-stop = keep existing sessions, avoid new pilot binds, start diagnostics capture.

dario: on observer->controller events: prefer push model. observer emits signed probe events with per-signal confidence. example event shape (controller can validate signature):
```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp-2026-42",
  "window_start": 1735554300,
  "duration_s": 120,
  "tenant_id": "tenant-17",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "signals": [
    {"name": "error_rate_delta", "value": 0.007, "confidence": 0.95},
    {"name": "p95_latency_mult", "value": 1.52, "confidence": 0.86}
  ],
  "summary": "error+latency anomaly",
  "observer_id": "obs-3",
  "signature": "sig-v1:..."
}
```
controller then applies policy rules + consults safety budget. provenance (observer-id, key-id) is required so controller trusts event.

julia: sketch of a compact policy yaml idea:
```yaml
soft_stop_policy:
  triggers:
    - name: error_rate_delta
      threshold: 0.005
      window: 180
    - name: p95_latency_mult
      threshold: 1.4
      window: 120
  actions:
    - name: soft_stop
      fallback_weight: 1.0  # fraction of new pilot traffic sent to fallback
      hold_for: 600         # seconds to hold soft-stop before re-eval
    - name: escalate_to_rollback
      after: 900            # seconds of continued violation to escalate
  cooldown: 600
  max_soft_stops_per_hour: 3
```
questions: should hold_for be tenant-configurable? should we allow partial fallback (e.g., fallback_weight 0.7) to reduce blast radius?

rahul: per-tenant overrides seem necessary for large customers. partial fallback helps limit disruption but complicates cache/KV warmup semantics. if router supports split routing + cache-warmup semantics, fallback_weight can be honored. otherwise default to binary (0 or 1).

maggie: ops needs: 1) audit trail for every soft-stop event, 2) automatic capture of diagnostics snapshot (recent requests, prompts, seeds), 3) queue a golden-check eval run. also clarify session-affinity: active sessions should remain on variant until end or TTL; document API semantics.

dario: edge cases:
- stateful streaming sessions cannot be silently moved mid-stream
- big-model cold starts: fallback may have different latency characteristics
- observer aggregation mistakes could trigger cascading soft-stops across tenants
recommend namespacing signals (tenant_id, region) and requiring observer aggregation granularity in event.

ops-bot: notice: deploy-controller v2.9 added 'soft_stop' primitive: POST /api/v2/rollouts/{id}/actions. rate-limit 10 reqs/min. docs: https://internal.redwood/rollouts#soft-stop

julia: who can override a soft-stop? proposal: autosystems (controller) can escalate to rollback, SRE oncall can force rollback, rollout owner or admins can force-continue. require higher confidence for auto-escalation (confidence floor), otherwise page humans. enforce 2FA & audit for manual force-continue.

rahul: add confidence floor for automatic rollback (e.g., aggregated confidence > 0.9). otherwise alert and keep soft-stop. include a manual 'force-continue' for owners with audit + 2FA.

maggie: add metric smoothing (EWMA) to reduce jitter. offer optional synthetic repro (small synthetic A/B with generated traffic) to verify after soft-stop (opt-in per rollout).

julia: next steps: i'll draft an RFC with event json spec, policy yaml, and controller state machine (states: ramping -> soft-stop -> escalate -> rollback -> recover). i'll ping for review next week. thanks all :sparkles:
